subject: Insurance
title: The Islamic Takaful Concept
description: A quick, practical guide to The Islamic Takaful Concept.

hook.text: Islamic traders developed 'takaful'—mutual guarantee. Merchants pooled funds; anyone hit by loss drew from the pool.

buildup.text: Conventional insurance involves selling risk for profit. Takaful avoids this by making all participants co-insurers.

discovery.text: Each member contributes to a shared fund. Surplus is returned to participants, not kept by a company.

twist.text: Today takaful is a $30 billion global industry. Ancient mutual aid became modern Islamic finance.

climax.text: Takaful proves insurance doesn't need a profit motive. Mutual aid works at modern scale when designed well.

punchline.text: Pool funds, share losses, return surplus. Takaful is mutual insurance.

quiz.question: How does takaful differ from conventional insurance?
options: Participants are co-insurers and surplus is shared
